Three ways to eat

Sit down, or take it home

The same kitchen feeds the dining room, the counter and every delivery app on the plateau.

Dine in

Booths and big tables under the gold folding-screen mural, with the bar through the doorway.

To go

The house to-go menu runs the whole kitchen. Two lines ring the same counter — one Tacoma, one Federal Way.

Delivered

They run on Uber Eats, DoorDash and Grubhub — the delivery orders are the best-rated thing they do.

The room

Old school, and still here

A Chinese kitchen in Milton Plaza that people have been ordering the same dish from for fifteen years and more.

The menu says Cantonese-Szechuan-Mandarin across the top, and it means it: almond fried chicken and sweet and sour pork sit a few lines from kung pao squid and Mongolian beef. Combination dinners come with tea and a fortune cookie. Family-style dinners are priced per person, minimum two orders — the way a big table has always ordered here.

The dining room hasn't chased a trend either. Green vinyl booths, a long gold folding-screen mural down one wall, and the bar through the doorway. It is the kind of place a town keeps.
